title: Transforming macromolecular structures into simulations of self-assembly with ioNERDSS.
authors: Ying, Yue Moon; Sang, Mankun; Au, Gabriel; Chhibber, Smriti; Du, Yufeng; Fischer, Jonathan A; Foley, Samuel L; Guo, Sikao; Herzog-Pohl, Ian; Liu, Zixiu; Roscom, Hannah; Sohail, Hassan; Takeshita, Sho S; Johnson, Margaret E
one_liner_zh: 该文开发ioNERDSS工具，将蛋白质静态结构转化为粗粒化模型并进行随机反应-扩散模拟，研究大分子自组装路径，结合ML预测结合亲和力，属于蛋白质结构计算建模与模拟的方法创新。
abstract: Macromolecular self-assembly is a fundamental process in living and engineered systems, producing molecular machines like the ribosome or highly symmetric viral capsids. Thanks to sources like the Protein Data Bank (PDB) and AlphaFold3, the final target complexes are often known, but these static structures do not provide information on the self-assembly process directly. Computational models provide critical tools to study these essential pathways of self-assembly, but substantial coarse graining of assembly subunits is necessary to achieve computational tractability of these relatively slow processes while retaining multi-valency. While local interactions overcome the often-prohibitive enumeration of all possible assembly intermediates, they must ensure global structural constraints are met. We here demonstrate ioNERDSS, a user-friendly Python package that transforms 3D atomic protein structures into coarse-grained (CG) models for immediate simulation with the stochastic reaction-diffusion NERDSS software, converting static structures into time-resolved assembly trajectories. With ioNERDSS, each protein chain is defined by a rigid subunit with discrete interfaces and explicit orientational constraints that enforce a structured assembly. Repeated subunits (such as in viral capsids) are regularized to preserve the target topology across distinct stochastic assembly pathways, supporting assembly of structures with thousands of subunits. We initialize pairwise binding affinities using ML prediction tools, and our default CG models are all constrained by thermodynamic reversibility to reach an equilibrium steady-state. The binding rates and subunit abundances necessary to perform simulations are initialized at default values but represent key variables that users should tune to test hypotheses on assembly pathways or to optimize models to experimental datasets. Benchmarking on over 50,000 PDB structures shows the majority of CG models will stochastically assemble into target structures. The ioNERDSS Python library links with open-source tools to facilitate fast and user-friendly structure validation and analysis of thermodynamic, kinetic, and nonequilibrium drivers of macromolecular self-assembly.
abstract_zh: 大分子自组装是生命系统和工程系统中的基本过程，产生诸如核糖体或高度对称的病毒衣壳等分子机器。得益于蛋白质数据银行（Protein Data Bank, PDB）和AlphaFold3等资源，最终目标复合物通常是已知的，但这些静态结构并不直接提供自组装过程的信息。计算模型为研究这些关键的自组装途径提供了重要工具，但为了在保持多价性的同时实现这些相对缓慢过程的计算可行性，必须对组装亚基进行大幅度的粗粒化处理。虽然局部相互作用克服了通常难以穷举的所有可能组装中间体的枚举问题，但它们必须确保满足全局结构约束。我们在此展示ioNERDSS，一个用户友好的Python包，它将3D原子蛋白质结构转化为粗粒化（coarse-grained, CG）模型，用于与随机反应-扩散NERDSS软件进行即时模拟，将静态结构转换为时间分辨的组装轨迹。通过ioNERDSS，每个蛋白质链被定义为一个具有离散界面和显式取向约束的刚性亚基，这些约束强制实现结构化组装。重复亚基（如病毒衣壳中的）被正则化，以在不同随机组装途径中保持目标拓扑结构，支持包含数千个亚基的结构组装。我们使用机器学习预测工具初始化成对结合亲和力，且我们的默认CG模型均受热力学可逆性约束，以达到平衡稳态。执行模拟所需的结合速率和亚基丰度以默认值初始化，但代表用户应调整的关键变量，以测试组装途径的假设或优化模型以适应实验数据集。对超过50,000个PDB结构的基准测试显示，大多数CG模型将随机组装成目标结构。ioNERDSS Python库与开源工具链接，以促进快速且用户友好的结构验证以及大分子自组装的热力学、动力学和非平衡驱动因素分析。
